title: Perf stand-down lifecycle edge cases
cluster_summary: These are separate per-repo lifecycle gaps, and no single upstream root fixes them. In each case, state armed before or during a stand-down (a Coalesce pending flag in LootHistory, a combat-held unlock in PanelMaster, a debug-hold timer in AbsorbTracker) outlives NS.StandDown. LH-R-04 and PM-R-06 are real bugs that players can see, cheap to fix locally, and should be addressed. The LibKa0s template's suspended=false is NOT dead: the current Perf host contract (rule 2, surface table) still endorses reading perf.suspended, and PartyFrameEnhanced and KickCD read it. So the upstream change is reduced to an optional comment refresh, and AT's vacuous assertion should be retargeted at NS.IsStoodDown(), not deleted along with the stub field.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed in core/Util.lua:249-268. pending=true is set before NS.After, and a canceled handle never runs the body that clears it, so the settings panel's RECORD_ADDED coalescer (built once) wedges for the rest of the session after a stand-down that lands within 0.2 s of a loot line. Players can see it and the fix is cheap.
verdicts.remediation: In Util.Coalesce, track the NS.After handle instead of a boolean and treat a canceled or absent handle as not pending. This also protects the Browser and Analytics coalescers. Add a test_util case 'a window canceled by the stand-down does not wedge the trigger' (red without the fix), then update the inventory and badge.

verdicts.assessment: pendingUnlock/pendingPanels (modules/Unlock.lua:18-19, 258) survive NS.StandDown. PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED is unregistered while the addon is down, so after a re-enable the next unrelated combat exit unlocks every panel. Disable and perf suspend are live verbs, so this is reachable mid-combat. There is no taint, but the behaviour surprises the player, and the fix is cheap.
verdicts.remediation: In NS.StandDown, drop the held queue (reuse the existing clear at Unlock.lua:245-249 or expose U:DropPending). Apply unlock state immediately while stood down. Correct the core/LifecycleSetup.lua:65-66 comment. Add a regression test: queue an unlock in combat, stand down, stand up, leave combat, and assert the panels stay locked.

verdicts.assessment: runHold gates only on the stored 'enabled' setting, so during a perf suspend it prints a false 'Holding...' line and arms a timer that outlives the stand-down's cancel. If the addon resumes before expiry, testHoldUntil can also briefly hold live repaints. Only a developer verb reaches it, and the effect is cosmetic.
verdicts.remediation: Gate runHold on NS.IsStoodDown(). Keep the DisabledLine for a disabled hold, and print a perf-suspended line otherwise. Add one case to tests/test_debughold.lua. Do this only alongside the other AbsorbTracker work in this run.

verdicts.assessment: The assertion at tests/test_perf.lua:538 reads back a stub literal the test itself set, so it cannot fail for ladder reasons. The proposed fix is wrong, though: dropping suspended from the stub reds tests/test_surface_parity.lua:253, and since the template field stays (see AT-R-08), deleting it would also diverge from the contract.
verdicts.remediation: Retarget the assertion at what the ladder reads, e.g. assertFalse(NS2.IsStoodDown(), 'and the show ladder sees a running addon'). Keep suspended=false in the core/PerfSetup.lua stub, keep the parity list unchanged, and regenerate the inventory.

verdicts.assessment: The premise 'a stub member nobody reads' is false. The current Perf doc's host contract rule 2 (l.491-492) and surface table (l.537) still direct hosts to consult perf.suspended, and PartyFrameEnhanced (Preview.lua:136/176, CastBars.lua:76, Slash.lua:209, Diagnostics.lua:94) and KickCD read it. Only the template's AT-specific comments are stale (l.352, l.386 say ShouldShowBar checks NS.Perf.suspended, but AT now asks the latch).
verdicts.remediation: Keep suspended=false in the template. As a doc-only change, refresh the comments at docs/api/Perf/version-14.1.1.6-docs.md l.352 and l.386 to say AT's ladder asks the lifecycle latch (NS.IsStoodDown). Optionally note under rule 2 that a latch-based host may ask the latch instead. No consumer-side 'drop the field' follow-up.
